title: Opening Chagigah: coming to see and to be seen
summary: The first shiur on Masechta Chagigah: who is exempt from going up to Yerushalayim for the Yom Tov, and why one blind in one eye is exempt, since as a person comes to see, so he comes to be seen. The two mutes who sat before Rebbe, Avraham as the first ger, why Torah is compared to water, and why the children were brought to Hakhel.
key_ideas: One who is blind in one eye is exempt from going up for the Yom Tov: as a person comes to see, so he comes to be seen.
Some have the custom of learning Masechta Chagigah on a yahrzeit.
Torah is compared to water, which flows from the highest place down to the lowest.
The children were brought to Hakhel so that those who bring them would earn reward.
